title: Small colimits of spaces and change of universe
statement: Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and smallness convention of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the spaces, coherent functors, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For either universe $\mathcal W$, write $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ for the infinity category presented by $\mathcal W$-small Kan complexes and their simplicial mapping complexes. Then $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ admits colimits of all diagrams indexed by $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets, including the empty diagram. Viewing a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex in $\mathcal U'$ induces a coherent fully faithful functor $\iota:\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$. For every $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set $K$, diagram $p:K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ and colimit cocone $p\to\Delta_K L$, its image $\iota p\to\Delta_K\iota L$ is a colimit cocone in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$. Change of universe is also compatible with the right-fibration models of presheaves: let $A$ be a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set and let a $\mathcal U$-small right fibration $q:E\to A$ classify $F:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ under space-valued transport with $\mathcal U$-small fibers. Then the same right fibration $q$, regarded in $\mathcal U'$, classifies $\iota\circ F:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$ under space-valued transport with $\mathcal U'$-small fibers, compatibly with the two mapping-space identifications $\operatorname{Map}(F,G)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/A}(E_F,E_G)$ for $\mathcal U$-small $G$. The categories of spaces themselves are formed in an auxiliary universe containing their objects.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.4.1 and Corollary 4.2.4.8, printed pp. 257 and 260 (PDF pp. 274 and 277), applied to the Kan model category of simplicial sets; universe invariance of the same small homotopy-colimit construction. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical universe-change result.

proof.text: Let $\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal W}$ be the simplicial category of $\mathcal W$-small Kan complexes, so that $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal W}$. The inclusion on objects and simplicial maps is an enriched functor: for small $X,Y$, its mapping complex in either universe has exactly the simplicial maps $X\times\Delta^n\to Y$ in degree $n$, with the same operators and composition. Applying the coherent nerve gives $\iota$. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] these complexes naturally represent the two infinity-categorical mapping spaces and the comparison respects enriched functors. Thus $\iota$ is fully faithful. In fact its coherent nerve is a full simplicial subset: an $n$-simplex is an enriched functor from $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, and when its objects are small all its mapping data already lie in $\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$. Everything is formed in a further auxiliary universe; this does not change these mapping complexes.

Check classification across universes by its actual construction, for any $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set $A$; no quasicategory hypothesis on $A$ is needed. Use the normalized classification by enriched evaluation and derived unstraightening specified in [lem-coef-universal-left-fibration-identity], with the right-fibration version given by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. By [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification], take a projectively cofibrant-fibrant strict diagram $P:\mathfrak C[A]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U}$ presenting $F:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ (use $\mathfrak C[A^{\mathrm{op}}]\cong\mathfrak C[A]^{\mathrm{op}}$). Unstraightening has simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to A$ equal to enriched natural maps $T_\sigma\to P$, where $T_\sigma$ is the cone-pushout diagram in the presentation node. Both $T_\sigma$ and $P$ are small. A natural map here is a family of functions between the same sets satisfying the same action equations; enlarging the universe adds no such functions. The cone pushout is likewise unchanged: its morphisms are finite composable words in the input morphisms modulo the relations identifying the common subcategory, degree by degree. Hence $U_A(P)$, its projection, its simplex operators, and its action on strict diagram maps are the same in both universes. Objectwise Kan fibrancy also persists, since each horn-filler problem is a problem between the same finite simplicial sets and $P(a)$. If a projective cofibrant replacement $P'\to P$ is needed in the larger universe, it is an objectwise weak equivalence between objectwise Kan diagrams. The presentation node makes $U_A(P')\to U_A(P)$ an equivalence of right fibrations. Enriched evaluation presents $P$ there by precisely $\iota F$, since its values, action maps and evaluation simplices have not changed; the replacement evaluates to a vertexwise equivalence and hence to a coherent equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Thus the same $U_A(P)$ classifies $\iota F$. By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], an arbitrary representative $E\to A$ of $F$ is equivalent over $A$ to $U_A(P)$. The inverse over-map and its two simplicial homotopies remain the same maps in the larger universe, so $E$ also classifies $\iota F$. All comparisons come from the same enriched evaluation, unstraightening and over-map compositions; inserting a parameter simplex gives the same comparison for every higher simplex. They therefore commute with the mapping-space identifications for two small representatives, not merely with their vertex fibers. For the covariant case, rectify a diagram $p:A\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ by a projectively cofibrant-fibrant $Q:\mathfrak C[A]\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U}$. Its normalized classifying left fibration is $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_A Q=(U_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}Q)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The cone and natural-map formulas just checked, now on the base $A^{\mathrm{op}}$, give the same $U_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}Q$ in both universes. Taking opposite simplicial sets changes only the indices of face and degeneracy maps, so the resulting left fibration is unchanged too. In the larger universe, a projective cofibrant-fibrant replacement $Q\prime\to Q$ evaluates to a vertexwise equivalence with $\iota p$; the covariant preservation-of-objectwise-equivalences clause of the presentation node identifies its unstraightening with this unchanged left fibration. By the normalization in the universal-left-fibration node it therefore classifies $\iota p$. For an arbitrary small representative, the over-maps and homotopies witnessing its equivalence to this model remain over-maps and homotopies in the larger universe. The mapping comparison is the right-derived comparison induced by enriched evaluation and unstraightening, followed by composition with these equivalences. Each small parameterized over-map $E\times\Delta^n\to E\prime$ is the same family of functions in both universes, and both precomposition and postcomposition are the same functions. Consequently the comparisons commute on mapping spaces, including the comparisons with constant products $A\times X$. In particular they take the transformation represented by a small over-map $E\to A\times X$ to the transformation represented by that very over-map in the larger universe. This verifies the cocone compatibility used below without asserting that taking opposites is a simplicial enriched functor.

source.place: Sections 2.2.1-2.2.3: cone-pushout straightening, its right adjoint and Theorem 2.2.1.2; Proposition 4.2.4.4: enriched-evaluation rectification. The explicit size comparison is supplied here.

proof.text: Let $K$ be a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set and $p:K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ a coherent diagram. By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], choose a $\mathcal U$-small left fibration $q:E\to K$ classifying $p$. Put $L=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}E$ and let $j:E\to L$ be its unit. By [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], $L$ is Kan and $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. It is small: each $\operatorname{Ex}$ degree is a set of maps from a finite subdivision simplex into the preceding small simplicial set, and the sequential colimit is a quotient of a countable union of small sets. The over-map $(q,j):E\to K\times L$, together with the constant-functor and mapping-space clauses of transport classification, gives a coherent cocone $\alpha:p\to\Delta_K L$. This defines the actual cocone rather than only choosing an apex.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.4.6 (the total left fibration models the colimit), with its cocone constructed using the classification of Section 2.2.1; Kan replacement is the cited explicit Ex-infinity construction.

proof.text:
For a small Kan test space $Y$, the preceding cocone induces the composite
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(L,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(L,Y)\xrightarrow{j^*}\operatorname{Fun}(E,Y)\cong\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(E,K\times Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(p,\Delta_KY).$$
The first equivalence is [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The second arrow is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance], applied to the weak homotopy equivalence $j$; this node explicitly allows a non-Kan $E$. The middle isomorphism sends $h$ to $(q,h)$, including on every parameter simplex. The final equivalence is the mapping-space and constant-functor clauses of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Its compatibility with composition identifies this whole composite with precomposition by $\alpha$: a map $f:L\to Y$ goes to $(q,fj)$, the composite of $(q,j)$ with $1_K\times f$. Therefore the dual cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves that $\alpha$ is colimiting. If $K$ is empty, so is $E$ and its Ex-infinity replacement, and all the displayed mapping spaces are terminal. This proves existence also for the empty diagram.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4.3 (cocone mapping-space criterion); Corollary 3.3.4.6 (total-space description), with the comparison map written out.

proof.text:
Now let $Y$ be any $\mathcal U'$-small Kan complex, with no $\mathcal U$-smallness restriction. Step 2 says the unchanged $q:E\to K$ classifies $\iota p$, and $(q,j)$ represents $\iota\alpha$, compatibly with mapping spaces and constant products. The construction $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}E$ is unchanged in the larger universe: in each degree its stages are the same sets of maps from subdivision simplices, and its sequential colimit is the same quotient of their disjoint union. Thus $j$ is also the Ex-infinity unit computed in $\mathcal U'$, and [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products] says there that $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. We have the chain
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}}(\iota L,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(L,Y)\xrightarrow{j^*}\operatorname{Fun}(E,Y)\cong\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(E,K\times Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'})}(\iota p,\Delta_KY).$$
The first comparison is [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The arrow $j^*$ is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance], whose hypotheses allow arbitrary simplicial $E$ and this larger Kan target $Y$. The middle isomorphism sends a parameterized map $h:E\times\Delta^n\to Y$ to $(q\circ\operatorname{pr}_E,h)$. The last equivalence is [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] in $\mathcal U'$. On a parameterized map $f:L\times\Delta^n\to Y$ the composite is the over-map $(q\circ\operatorname{pr}_E,f\circ(j\times\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^n}))$. Compatibility of classification with composition therefore identifies it with precomposition by $\iota\alpha$. The dual criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves that $\iota\alpha$ is a colimit cocone, since this induced map is an equivalence for every larger test space $Y$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4.3 and the total-space construction of Corollary 3.3.4.6, now tested against larger Kan complexes; universe comparison from step 2.

proof.text: Finally take any colimit cocone $\lambda:p\to\Delta_K L_0$ in the statement. By the dual initial-object and cocone criteria of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $\alpha$ and $\lambda$ are initial objects of the same cocone quasicategory. There are maps of cocones in both directions; each composite is homotopic to the corresponding identity because its mapping space out of an initial object is contractible. Their apex maps give an equivalence $e:L\simeq L_0$ with the specified homotopy $e\alpha\simeq\lambda$. Applying $\iota$ preserves these inverse maps and homotopies. For every larger test $Y$, precomposition by $\iota e$ identifies the universal-arrow map for $\iota\lambda$ with the universal-arrow map for $\iota\alpha$ of step 5. The former is consequently an equivalence, so $\iota\lambda$ is colimiting by the same criterion. This proves preservation for the given cocone, not only for the chosen model.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4.3; uniqueness of initial objects in the cocone category. This last step is the written-out inverse-and-homotopy argument.

proof_origin.place: Sections 2.2.1-2.2.3, Proposition 4.2.4.4, Lemma 4.2.4.3, Corollaries 3.3.4.6 and 4.2.4.8; online source read, explicit universe comparison and total-space mapping proof supplied by Q10.
